deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft for Riemann's 1861 memoir 'Ein Beitrag zu den Untersuchungen über die Bewegung eines flüssigen gleichartigen Ellipsoides'. It treats Dirichlet's problem of a homogeneous, self-gravitating fluid ellipsoid whose particle coordinates are linear in the initial coordinates. The page has kinematic and dynamic set-up only.

(0) Upper right corner: a non-mathematical motto signed F. A. Wolf, the classical philologist. It reads roughly: 'Due love to all the studies dear to you, and to the young men entrusted to you; in case of conflict, however, the greater love to the latter.'

(1) Lagrangian linear motion. Let X0 = (x0/a0, y0/b0, z0/c0)^T, where a0, b0, c0 are the initial semi-axes. Then x = M(t) X0, with M = [[l,m,n],[l',m',n'],[l'',m'',n'']]. The initial ellipsoid |X0| = 1 is carried to an ellipsoid at every time.

(2) Body axes. ξ = R x, where R is orthogonal with rows (α,β,γ), (α',β',γ'), (α'',β'',γ''). So (ξ,η,ζ) are coordinates along the instantaneous principal axes.

(4) Internal motion. (ξ/a, η/b, ζ/c)^T = S X0, where S is a second orthogonal matrix with entries α1, β1, γ1, ... and a, b, c are the current semi-axes.

(3) Since S is orthogonal, ξ²/a² + η²/b² + ζ²/c² = x0²/a0² + y0²/b0² + z0²/c0². Hence the particles on the boundary stay on the boundary.

(5) Combining (2) and (4): M = R^T diag(a,b,c) S. This is a singular-value-type decomposition of the deformation matrix. It gives:
- l = M11 = aαα1 + bα'α1' + cα''α1''
- m = M12 = aαβ1 + bα'β1' + cα''β1''
- l' = M21 = aβα1 + bβ'α1' + cβ''α1''

Equations of motion (Euler/Dirichlet form). Project the Lagrangian equations onto the ξ, η, ζ directions:
- Σ ẍ_i ∂x_i/∂ξ − 2∂V/∂ξ + ∂p/∂ξ = 0, and likewise for η and ζ.
- The factor 2 reflects Riemann's normalisation of the potential V.
- Since x = R^T ξ, we have ∂x/∂ξ = α, ∂y/∂ξ = β, ∂z/∂ξ = γ. So the first equation reads αẍ + βÿ + γz̈ = 2∂V/∂ξ − ∂p/∂ξ, as in the line on the right.

Rotating-frame kinematics. Define the angular velocities of the axes:
- p = α̇'α'' + β̇'β'' + γ̇'γ''
- q = α̇''α + β̇''β + γ̇''γ
- r = α̇α' + β̇β' + γ̇γ' = −(αα̇' + ββ̇' + γγ̇')

Then Ω = Ṙ R^T = [[0,r,−q],[−r,0,p],[q,−p,0]]. From dξ/dt = Ω ξ + R ẋ, the body components of the velocity are:
- ξ' = αẋ + βẏ + γż = dξ/dt − rη + qζ
- η' = dη/dt + rξ − pζ
- ζ' = dζ/dt − qξ + pη

The acceleration components are R ẍ = d(Rẋ)/dt − Ω(Rẋ). The first is αẍ + βÿ + γz̈ = dξ'/dt − rη' + qζ'. All of this appears twice on the page: first with letters u, v, w for p, q, r (left), then cleanly with p, q, r (right).

Internal rotation. For fixed X0, d(ξ/a)/dt = w1 η/b − v1 ζ/c, i.e. Ṡ S^T = [[0,w1,−v1],[−w1,0,u1],[v1,−u1,0]]. Riemann later renames this r1, q1 (p1). Hence:
- dξ/dt = ȧ ξ/a + a w1 η/b − a v1 ζ/c
- ξ' = ȧ ξ/a + (a w1 − b w) η/b + (c v − a v1) ζ/c

The page writes (a v1 − c w) for the last coefficient; see errors. The same expression is restarted at the bottom ('ξ' = ∂a/∂t ξ/a + ...') in the r, q notation.

Forces. V = H − Aξ² − Bη² − Cζ² is the interior potential of the homogeneous ellipsoid, with A, B, C the standard elliptic integrals. The pressure ansatz is p = P + G(1 − ξ²/a² − η²/b² − ζ²/c²), vanishing on the surface when P = 0. Then 2∂V/∂ξ − ∂p/∂ξ = −4Aξ + 2Gξ/a², and similarly for η and ζ.

Purpose. Equating the coefficients of ξ, η, ζ in the projected equations yields Riemann's ODE system for a, b, c, p, q, r, u1, v1, w1, G. The next page then studies stationary cases, for example (b−a)vw + ... = 0 and b² = a²(3a²−c²)/(a²+c²), i.e. Riemann ellipsoids.
errors: The final coefficient in ξ' = ∂a/∂t ξ/a + (a w1 − b w)η/b + (a v1 − c w)ζ/c should be (c v − a v1)ζ/c. This follows from dξ/dt = ȧξ/a + a w1 η/b − a v1 ζ/c combined with ξ' = dξ/dt − wη + vζ. As read, the sign is reversed and w appears where v belongs. This is a draft slip, possibly partly a reading issue.

The left draft lines ∂η/∂t = −w1 ξ + ḃη/b + u1 ζ/c and ∂ζ/∂t = v1 ξ − u1 η + ċ ζ omit scale factors. They should be ∂η/∂t = −b w1 ξ/a + ḃη/b + b u1 ζ/c and ∂ζ/∂t = c v1 ξ/a − c u1 η/b + ċ ζ/c. These are scratch lines that Riemann abandoned.
Line 'q = α' and the expression '= wφ + ∂η/∂t − uη' are unfinished or unclear fragments. The three equations at the bottom right (∂(ξ/a)/∂t = r1 η/b − q1 ζ/c, ...) are left incomplete.
The factor 2 in front of ∂V/∂ξ is a normalisation convention, not an error. Labels (3) and (2) appear out of order.

results.what: Dirichlet's linear (affine) motion of a fluid ellipsoid, x = M(t) X0, with boundary preservation
Decomposition M = R^T diag(a,b,c) S into two orthogonal matrices and the semi-axes
results.modern_name: Singular value decomposition of the deformation gradient (rotation of figure axes plus internal circulation)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann 1861 for this hydrodynamic use; SVD generally to Beltrami 1873 and Jordan 1874

results.what: Velocity and acceleration components in a rotating frame with angular velocities p, q, r
results.modern_name: Euler kinematics in rotating frames (Ω = Ṙ R^T)

results.what: Interior potential of a homogeneous ellipsoid, quadratic in the coordinates, and the quadratic pressure ansatz
results.modern_name: Ellipsoidal potential (Maclaurin/Gauss/Dirichlet) and the Dirichlet pressure law

results.what: Set-up of equations leading to steady 'Riemann ellipsoids' (worked out on the next page)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working draft of the set-up of Riemann's published 1861 ellipsoid memoir: the decomposition into two rotations and the semi-axes, and the rotating-frame equations. All of this is well known as his. The only incidental novelty is the F. A. Wolf motto.

checkable.sympy: from sympy import *; th,ph,a,b,c=symbols('th ph a b c'); R=rot_axis3(th); S=rot_axis1(ph); M=R.T*diag(a,b,c)*S; al,be,ga=R.row(0); al1,al1p,al1pp=S.col(0); alp,bep,gap=R.row(1); alpp,bepp,gapp=R.row(2); simplify(M[0,0]-(a*R[0,0]*S[0,0]+b*R[1,0]*S[1,0]+c*R[2,0]*S[2,0]))==0
checkable.asserts: l = aαα1 + bα'α1' + cα''α1'' follows from M = R^T diag(a,b,c) S
the formulas for m and l' (5)
(3): ξ²/a²+η²/b²+ζ²/c² = x0²/a0²+y0²/b0²+z0²/c0² since S is orthogonal
Ṙ R^T is antisymmetric, so r = Σα̇α' = −Σαα̇' etc.

checkable.sympy: x=Matrix([Function(n)(t) for n in 'xyz']); xi=R*x; simplify(R*x.diff(t) - (xi.diff(t) - Om*xi))==zeros(3,1)
checkable.asserts: body velocity components ξ' = dξ/dt − rη + qζ etc., with r = Om[0,1], −q = Om[0,2], p = Om[1,2]

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,w,v,w1,v1,ad,eta,zeta,xi=symbols('a b c w v w1 v1 ad eta zeta xi'); dxi=ad*xi/a+a*w1*eta/b-a*v1*zeta/c; expand(dxi-w*eta+v*zeta-(ad*xi/a+(a*w1-b*w)*eta/b+(c*v-a*v1)*zeta/c))==0
checkable.asserts: correct form of ξ'; the coefficient of ζ/c is (c v − a v1), not (a v1 − c w) as written

transcription_corrections: Motto line 1 likely reads 'Gebührende Liebe zu all den Studien, die Dir theuer [?] sind, und zu den Jünglingen, die Dir anvertraut sind; bei Collisionen aber die grössere Liebe zu den Letzteren. F. A. Wolf' rather than 'die die trauliche'.
In ∂ζ/∂t = v1ξ − u1η + ∂c/∂t ζ the last term is presumably ∂c/∂t·ζ/c, a scratch slip on the page.
'= wφ + ∂η/∂t − uη' is likely '= wξ' + ∂η'/∂t − uζ'' (the η-component of acceleration in u, v, w notation).
The equations of motion use d²x/dt² (total) times ∂x/∂ξ; the first right-hand side reads 2∂V/∂ξ − ∂p/∂ξ, with the crossed-out term being 2∂V/∂ξ.
